narration: Kangeelu: The Coconut Leaf Dance of Spirits
This is Kangeelu. traditional, ongoing.
on_screen: Title card: Kangeelu · India · traditional, ongoing

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Kangeelu originates from the Udupi and Dakshina Kannada regions of Karnataka, India, performed by the mundaala community.
It is linked to the Tulu calendar's Mai month and is part of a seven-day festival to propitiate goddess Khadgeshwari and Koragajja, a spirit form of Shiva.
The dance has spiritual roots aimed at protecting the village from disease and evil forces.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Performed on the full moon day of the Mai month (March), Kangeelu is a spiritual dance to ward off disease, evil spirits, and negative energy.
It fosters peace, harmony, and community spirit.
The dance is part of a seven-day ritual festival and includes a procession of the goddess Khadgeshwari's wooden statue and a communal feast.
Today it is a living tradition.

narration: Watch for Koragajja Dance.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music includes folk songs called Karungilo and Aati Kalenje, sung by four singers wearing bells in the center of the circle.
Percussion instruments like Kaase or Dholu provide the rhythmic beats.
Listen for the Kaase, Dholu, bells.
Percussive drum beats with bell accompaniment underpin folk vocal songs sung in a call-and-response style, creating a rhythmic and spiritual atmosphere.
on_screen: Instrument names on screen as each is mentioned

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers wear heavy, colorful dresses made from the tender top growth of coconut trees and palm leaves, with face paint.
One dancer wears a mask and black body paint to represent Koragajja.
The dance takes place in a village setting, often outdoors, with a circle formation and a central group of singers.
on_screen: Reconstruction imagery allowed only from the costume notes, labelled 'reconstruction'

scenes.title: The people
narration: Koragajja, a spirit considered a form of god Shiva, is central to the dance.
The goddess Khadgeshwari is propitiated through the ritual.
In Dakshina Kannada, men perform the dance, while in Udupi, women perform it.
Kangeelu is a traditional Indian folk dance belonging to the Tulu-speaking communities of Karnataka.
